messages:
aj: heads-up — p95 for /v1/generate tile jumps ~180ms when I enable the deployment_cohort rollup in staging. saw it twice with different test cohorts, reproducible.

sam: can you share the query and a screenshot? :eyes:

aj: Screenshot omitted. Query I ran:
```
SELECT merge_percentiles(rollup_tdigest) AS pcts
FROM namespace.rollups
WHERE route = '/v1/generate' AND window = '5m'
GROUP BY deployment_cohort
```
Toggling the cohort-ordering flag in the console swaps which cohort gets merged first and the p95 shifts.

kumi: that smells like centroid-ordering non-determinism in incremental tdigest merges. Did you compare incremental-merge vs rebuild-from-samples?

aj: yes. incremental merge shows the jump; a full rebuild from raw samples gives stable p50/p95/p99 across runs.

ben: are these compressed rollups or raw blobs? we compress at ingest with comp=100.

aj: compressed blobs. I dumped two rollups: cohort A (lots of short requests) and cohort B (sparse heavy tail). Merging A->B vs B->A changes the interpolation in the merged tdigest, producing the p95 delta.

maria: ok short list of actionables: (1) add unit/integration tests that merge rollups in both orders and assert percentiles equal, (2) introduce a deterministic merge ordering (e.g., stable sort by centroid mean or cohort id) as a guard, (3) document and expose merge-mode metadata so operators can choose rebuild for SLO-backed rollups.

sam: proposal: include rollup metadata fields merge_mode: "incremental"|"rebuild" and merge_seed: "hex". Console shows merge_mode on the latency tile metadata panel.

kumi: prototype: sorting centroids by mean before reduce fixes the sign but increases memory and CPU. Rebuild-from-samples is most correct but 3-4x CPU.

aj: local perf numbers: centroid-sort adds ~30% to wall time on large rollups and ~20% more memory; full rebuild is ~3-4x CPU but gives bit-for-bit stable percentiles.

ben: for SLO surfaces I'd side with correctness. We could default SLO-tagged rollups to rebuild in the recompute job and keep incremental for ad-hoc cheap rollups.

maria: agreed. UX: show an annotation on the tile: "merge-mode: rebuild (deterministic)" or "merge-mode: incremental (cost-optimized)" with a tooltip: "Incremental merges may introduce small percentile jitter. Use rebuild for SLOs. See PLAT-1321."

deploy-bot: Deployed canary patch aj/centroid-stable-sort to staging at 1799999015. Rollout: 10%.

metrics-bot: Alert "p95-flap-investigation" muted for 30m while we investigate.

sam: also file a docs ticket to explain expected jitter magnitudes and how to interpret p95 blips. PLAT-1321?

aj: opened PLAT-1321 with repro matrix, perf tradeoffs, and sample dumps. linked test vectors. PR for tests coming shortly.

maria: good. For short term: implement deterministic sort in merge path + surface merge_mode in UI. Longer term: evaluate adaptive rebuild for SLO-tagged rollups during low-traffic windows.

kumi: I'll mock up the tile metadata UI to include merge_mode and a copyable link to the rollup metadata JSON so oncall can reproduce exact merge order.

aj: thanks. I'll push the unit tests and the small sort patch. will post perf numbers before we flip the default in prod. keeping this thread updated.
